title: SEC2: no efficiency issues in peer_whitelist
description:
Reviewed crates/smtp/Cargo.toml, crates/smtp/src/config.rs, and crates/smtp/src/session.rs for epic stoa-1d9d418c (manual peer whitelist).

No measurable efficiency issues found.

Specific checks performed:

1. peer_whitelist scan (session.rs:191-194): config.peer_whitelist.iter().any(...) is called once per connection at session setup, not in the per-command loop. O(n) over n=0-10 entries; trivially fast and structurally correct.

2. IpNet::contains (session.rs:194): O(1) bitmask comparison per ipnet crate implementation. No concern.

3. Allocations in hot path: zero. client_ip is an IpAddr (Copy), IpNet values are borrowed from the Arc<Config>. The whitelist check allocates nothing.

4. peer_addr parsed once (session.rs:171-185): SocketAddr parse is done once into client_ip; that value is reused for both the whitelist check and the later verify_inbound call. No redundant parsing.

5. connection_whitelisted dead write (session.rs:198): The bool is computed and then suppressed with let _ = .... The compiler elides the pure computation at opt level. The tracing::info! at line 196 does execute on whitelisted connections, but that is a connection-setup path and acceptable. The comment explains this is placeholder until greylisting (stoa-ef702cf6) consumes the flag.

6. T1-T8 test helpers (config.rs:790-811): whitelist_check re-parses CIDR strings on each call. Acceptable for a test helper; production code holds pre-parsed Vec<IpNet>. No production efficiency concern.

All checks pass. Implementation is clean for the stated scale (0-10 whitelist entries, connection-granularity check).
